title: The star cluster and nebula NGC 371
caption: The star cluster and nebula NGC 371, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 371 · constellation Tucana · about 200000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The star cluster NGC 371 and the nebula that surrounds it were captured by the FORS1 instrument from ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile, where it was mounted on the Very Large Telescope.

NGC 371 is not in the Milky Way. Its home is the Small Magellanic Cloud, a close galactic neighbor. Studying clusters in a neighboring galaxy lets astronomers compare star formation there with what happens at home.

A star cluster wrapped in a nebula is typically a place where stars have formed out of the surrounding clouds of gas. Young, hot stars give off energetic light that makes nearby gas glow. The filters used for this image isolate light from helium and hydrogen, the kinds of emission such glowing gas produces.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.90 x 6.91 arcminutes) and distance (200000 light years), the frame spans roughly 401 × 402 light-years. Its light set out about 200,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: FORS1 on the Very Large Telescope imaged this scene through narrow filters that isolate ionized helium, neutral helium and hydrogen-alpha light. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The narrow filters pick out light from specific gases, and the long exposures reveal faint nebula glow the eye could not see in another galaxy.
